structures.overall_structure: Precipitation transformation (labelled 'generic precipitation transformation'): γ passed through a more complex random-like transformation, not as ordered and defined as discontinuous precipitation; reactions involved the whole γ volume. γ + κ-carbide lamellar structures were NOT detected; instead an austenite matrix featured by carbon-depleted γ regions with globular κ-carbides, plus alternated bands of two different austenite grades.

unmapped_findings: For 12Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C the γ phase underwent a 'generic precipitation transformation' (complex random-like, not as ordered as discontinuous precipitation) that was linked to only slight/incipient hardening (Table 4: hot-rolled 401 HV → 600 °C tempered 420 HV, i.e. +19 HV).

In 12Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C, γ + κ-carbide lamellar structures were NOT detected; instead an austenite matrix with carbon-depleted γ regions and globular κ-carbides formed, accompanied by strong κ-carbide precipitation along δ/γ boundaries and poor κ-carbide precipitation within ferrite. The absence of random lamellar phases was stated to ensure a more solid microstructure configuration.
At 12% Al the 600 °C reactions involved the whole γ volume (contrasted with the corresponding 9% Al heat-treated alloy, Fig. 1(a), where austenite grains only partially transformed).

Fig. 4 is captioned as precipitation transformation in 600 °C tempered 12Al-10Mn-1C and its BSE-SEM panel labels read 'γ+κ lamellae' and 'γα+coarse κ'; however, the paired EDS table in the same figure group is titled 'EDS for Al and Mn in 9Al-10Mn-1C tempered at 600 °C', so the figure caption alloy and the table-title alloy disagree (data ambiguity noted, not assigned to this sample).

The paper reports that precipitation transformation produced microstructures featuring fine/coarse γ + κ-carbide lamellae and carbon-depleted γ-bands + κ-carbide nodules (conclusions, general to the transformation type).
Minitab18® software was used to verify consistency of the acquired data and outliers were excluded from the investigation.

No tensile, ductility, density, thermal, corrosion or other quantitative property values were reported specifically for the 12Al-10Mn-1C alloy in the 600 °C tempered condition; only Vickers hardness (420 HV) is given.
